records.context: **CORUM % and KEGG %**, the share of clusters with at least one enriched group: a two-sided Fisher exact test for every group in every cluster, Benjamini-Hochberg within the cluster, enriched at FDR < 0.05. The background is every clustered row, non-targeting rows included. Two variants are reported: ``may2025`` counts every member of a group (Brieflow's release of May 2025, which reproduces Funk et al.'s 24.3 % and 13.5 %) and ``head`` only the members in the background (Brieflow's current code).
records.label: spacr.ops_clusters#3
records.source: **CORUM % and KEGG %**, the share of clusters with at least one enriched group: a two-sided Fisher exact test for every group in every cluster, Benjamini-Hochberg within the cluster, enriched at FDR < 0.05. The background is every clustered row, non-targeting rows included. Two variants are reported: ``may2025`` counts every member of a group (Brieflow's release of May 2025, which reproduces Funk et al.'s 24.3 % and 13.5 %) and ``head`` only the members in the background (Brieflow's current code).
records.translation: **CORUM % y KEGG %**, la proporción de clústeres con al menos un grupo enriquecido: una prueba exacta de Fisher bilateral para cada grupo en cada clúster, Benjamini-Hochberg dentro del clúster, con enriquecimiento a FDR < 0.05. Se informan dos variantes: ``may2025`` cuenta todos los miembros de un grupo (la versión de Brieflow de mayo de 2025, que reproduce el 24.3 % y el 13.5 % de Funk et al.) y ``head`` solo los miembros presentes en el fondo (el código actual de Brieflow).

records.context: :func:`spacr.gene_measurement_compare.mitotic_calls` calls a cell mitotic with a fixed rule on nuclear DNA intensity and area. On plate A of Funk et al. 2022 the per-gene mitotic index from that rule correlates with Funk et al.'s at Spearman rho = 0.32 only. records.label: spacr.ops_mitotic#1
records.source: :func:`spacr.gene_measurement_compare.mitotic_calls` calls a cell mitotic with a fixed rule on nuclear DNA intensity and area. records.translation: :func:`spacr.gene_measurement_compare.mitotic_calls` clasifica una célula como mitótica con una regla fija basada en la intensidad y el área del DNA nuclear. En la placa A de Funk et al. 2022, el índice mitótico por gen obtenido con esa regla se correlaciona con el de Funk et al. con un rho de Spearman = 0.32 solamente. Funk et al. entrenaron en su lugar un clasificador con características de DNA y de tubulina; este módulo hace lo mismo con células etiquetadas.

records.context: The steps, with the batch being the microplate sample position:
records.label: spacr.ops_tvn#2
records.source: The steps, with the batch being the well:
records.translation: Los pasos, siendo el lote el pocillo:

records.context: 1. columns with more than ``max_nonfinite`` non-finite values are dropped and the remaining gaps are filled with the column median; 2. every batch is centred and scaled on all of its cells; 3. a PCA keeping ``pca_variance`` of the variance is fitted on a random sample of ``pca_sample`` cells (seed ``seed``) and every cell is projected; 4. the projection is centred and scaled on the control cells, rotated onto the principal axes of the control cells, and every axis is scaled to unit variance on the control cells of each batch (the whitening); 5. CORAL aligns the control covariance of every batch to the pooled one (both regularised by ``coral_ridge`` times the identity).
records.label: spacr.ops_tvn#3
records.source: 1. columns with more than ``max_nonfinite`` non-finite values are dropped and the remaining gaps are filled with the column median; 2. every batch is centred and scaled on all of its cells; 3. a PCA keeping ``pca_variance`` of the variance is fitted on a random sample of ``pca_sample`` cells (seed ``seed``) and every cell is projected; 4. the projection is centred and scaled on the control cells, rotated onto the principal axes of the control cells, and every axis is scaled to unit variance on the control cells of each batch (the whitening); 5. CORAL aligns the control covariance of every batch to the pooled one (both regularised by ``coral_ridge`` times the identity).
records.translation: 1. se descartan las columnas con más de ``max_nonfinite`` valores no finitos y los huecos restantes se rellenan con la mediana de la columna; 2. cada lote se centra y escala sobre todas sus células; 3. una PCA que conserva ``pca_variance`` de la varianza se ajusta sobre una muestra aleatoria de ``pca_sample`` células (semilla ``seed``) y se proyecta cada célula; 4. la proyección se centra y escala sobre las células de control, se rota sobre los ejes principales de las células de control y cada eje se escala a varianza unitaria sobre las células de control de cada lote (el blanqueamiento); 5. CORAL alinea la covarianza de los controles de cada lote con la combinada (ambas regularizadas con ``coral_ridge`` veces la identidad).

records.context: Two implementations are given. :func:`tvn_in_memory` holds every cell at once, as Brieflow does. :func:`fit_tvn_streamed` reads one batch at a time and keeps only the control cells and a PCA sample, so a laboratory microplate or a pool of laboratory microplates never sits in memory; :meth:`TVNModel.transform` then applies the fitted model batch by batch.
records.label: spacr.ops_tvn#4
records.source: Two implementations are given. :func:`tvn_in_memory` holds every cell at once, as Brieflow does. :func:`fit_tvn_streamed` reads one batch at a time and keeps only the control cells and a PCA sample, so a plate or a pool of plates never sits in memory; :meth:`TVNModel.transform` then applies the fitted model batch by batch.
records.translation: Se ofrecen dos implementaciones. :func:`tvn_in_memory` mantiene todas las células a la vez, como hace Brieflow. :func:`fit_tvn_streamed` lee un lote cada vez y conserva solo las células de control y una muestra para la PCA, de modo que nunca hay una placa ni un conjunto de placas en memoria; después :meth:`TVNModel.transform` aplica el modelo ajustado lote a lote.

records.context: The whitening makes the low-variance tail sensitive to the PCA fit sample. Step 4 divides every axis by its control spread, so an axis that holds almost no control variance is blown up to the same weight as the first one. Which weak directions survive step 3 depends on the cells in the PCA sample, so two fits that differ only in that sample (or in the order the batches are read) agree on the strong axes but not on the tail. On laboratory microplate A of Funk et al. 2022 the in-memory and the streamed fits give gene-pair cosines that correlate at only r = 0.82, while their string auprc is the same. ``whiten_epsilon`` is added to every axis's control variance at both scaling steps (``x / sqrt(var + epsilon)`` instead of ``x / sqrt(var)``), which shrinks the weak axes: at 3, the default, the two fits correlate at r = 0.93 and the string auprc is at or above Brieflow's. ``whiten_epsilon=0`` is Brieflow's TVN exactly, the setting that reproduces the laboratory microplate A pilot. ``components`` keeps only the leading control axes; it did not help on laboratory microplate A and is off by default.

Step 4 divides every axis by its control spread, so an axis that holds almost no control variance is blown up to the same weight as the first one. Which weak directions survive step 3 depends on the cells in the PCA sample, so two fits that differ only in that sample (or in the order the batches are read) agree on the strong axes but not on the tail. On plate A of Funk et al. 2022 the in-memory and the streamed fits give gene-pair cosines that correlate at only r = 0.82, while their STRING AUPRC is the same. ``whiten_epsilon`` is added to every axis's control variance at both scaling steps (``x / sqrt(var + epsilon)`` instead of ``x / sqrt(var)``), which shrinks the weak axes: at 3, the default, the two fits correlate at r = 0.93 and the STRING AUPRC is at or above Brieflow's. ``whiten_epsilon=0`` is Brieflow's TVN exactly, the setting that reproduces the plate A pilot. ``components`` keeps only the leading control axes; it did not help on plate A and is off by default.
records.translation: EL BLANQUEAMIENTO HACE QUE LA COLA DE BAJA VARIANZA SEA SENSIBLE A LA MUESTRA DE AJUSTE DE LA PCA. El paso 4 divide cada eje por la dispersión de sus controles, de modo que un eje que apenas contiene varianza de los controles se amplifica hasta el mismo peso que el primero. Qué direcciones débiles sobreviven al paso 3 depende de las células de la muestra de la PCA, de modo que dos ajustes que solo difieren en esa muestra (o en el orden en que se leen los lotes) coinciden en los ejes fuertes pero no en la cola. En la placa A de Funk et al. 2022, los ajustes en memoria y en flujo dan cosenos entre pares de genes que solo se correlacionan con r = 0.82, mientras que su AUPRC de STRING es la misma. ``whiten_epsilon`` se suma a la varianza de los controles de cada eje en ambos pasos de escalado (``x / sqrt(var + epsilon)`` en lugar de ``x / sqrt(var)``), lo que reduce los ejes débiles: con 3, el valor predeterminado, los dos ajustes se correlacionan con r = 0.93 y el AUPRC de STRING iguala o supera al de Brieflow. ``whiten_epsilon=0`` es exactamente la TVN de Brieflow, el ajuste que reproduce el piloto de la placa A. ``components`` conserva solo los ejes de control principales; no ayudó en la placa A y está desactivado por defecto.
